shots.say: Pour yourself something and settle in.
This one goes back centuries.
Eggnog started in medieval Britain as posset,
a hot milky drink made with ale, eggs, and spices reserved
for monks and the wealthy. A drink of good fortune
saved for special occasions. When it crossed
the Atlantic, colonists swap expensive European spirits
for cheap Caribbean rum, fresh farm eggs, and milk.
Eggnog went from a luxury drink to the holiday drink for everyone.
By the 18th century, it was flowing freely
at every Christmas gathering in the colonies.
George Washington served his guests an eggnog loaded with
brandy, rye whiskey, rum, and sherry
at Mount Vernon. His recipe ended with one final instruction,
taste frequently, solid advice.
In 1826, West Point cadets loved their eggnog so much
that when alcohol was banned on campus, they smuggled in whiskey anyway.
The holiday party turned into what history now calls the eggnog riot. Yes, that is true.
20 cadets were expelled, zero regrets, presumably.
This spiced eggnog adds American Heritage Chocolate crafted from an authentic 1700s recipe
to that centuries-old tradition.
Warm spices, rich chocolate, and 300 years of holiday history in every sip.
Some traditions are worth keeping.
